subject: DataFest visualization challenge on CA propositions - enter now! (due Nov 1)

messages.author: 2937cefa7be1be8e
messages.subject: DataFest visualization challenge on CA propositions - enter now! (due Nov 1)
parts:
Dear D-RUG,


We're running a little DataFest visualization challenge at the Data Science Initiative and have room for a few more teams. I invite you to participate! Event date for presenting your team's viz is next Thursday, Nov 1 from 2-3pm in the DSI. Teams can be undergrads or grads/postdocs. See details, below, and feel free to contact me or Jane with any questions. All are welcome to attend the final presentation session on Nov 1.


Election day is coming up and this year there are ELEVEN propositions on the ballot.  To make our civic duty more enjoyable and get some data science practice, the Data Science Initiative is hosting an invite-only visualizations focused DataFest to get ready.


To participate, claim a propositions here. Act fast to make sure that you get the proposition that you want! Only one team is allowed per proposition to compete, but we encourage all who are interested to try the challenge on their own.


Create ONE data visualization that helps explain the issue. It can be any type you want, and you're encouraged to try a new type of visualization or software. You can use any type of data from anywhere that is available to you. (See here and here and here for inspiration.) Make sure that your visualization is replicable. Teams can be 1-3 people per proposition.


Presentations are on Thursday, Nov 1st from 2-3pm in the DSI (Shields 360). To compete, present an overview of your selected proposition (including pros and cons) and your visualization in under 5 minutes. (Reading the state vote guide and a couple newspaper articles is a good place to start for preparing the overview.) Use no more than 2 slides for your presentation, and include a link to your repo with the data, code, etc. on the sign up sheet. Email your presentation slides to plrey...@ucdavis.edu BEFORE 2pm on Nov 1st to compete.


Vote! The best presentation will win a prize. You must be present at the Nov 1 meeting to win. All are welcome to attend the presentations.


Questions? Email plrey...@ucdavis.edu or jaca...@ucdavis.edu.
